Troops of Operation Enduring Peace have arrested two suspects over an attack on vigilante operatives and the subsequent burning of their office in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The suspects were arrested at about 1:40am on October 27, 2026, in the NEPA area of Jos North by troops of Sector 1 of the operation. The Media Information Officer of Operation Enduring Peace, Capt. Chinonso Oteh, confirmed the arrest while speaking to journalists in Jos on Wednesday. Oteh said the suspects were linked to the attack on vigilante personnel and the subsequent arson of their office. “The arrest followed allegations linking the suspects to the attack on vigilante personnel and the subsequent setting ablaze of their office,” he said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources He disclosed that the suspects were in custody for further investigation and necessary action. According to him, the arrest was part of ongoing efforts by OPEP to tackle criminal activities and sustain peace across the state. Oteh assured residents that security personnel would intensify operations to identify and apprehend individuals involved in activities capable of undermining peace and security. Seven die as gunmen invade Plateau community Police probe Edo vigilante caught extorting motorists Mutfwang vows arrest of Plateau attacks masterminds He also urged residents to support security agencies by providing credible information that could help prevent crime and facilitate the arrest of suspects. “We call on members of the public to cooperate with the military and other security agencies by providing timely and credible information that could assist in preventing criminal activities and apprehending suspects,” he said. He added that public cooperation remained crucial to maintaining peace and security across Plateau State. On Monday, the troops of Operation Enduring Peace arrested a suspected fake soldier in the Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State for alleged phone snatching and public disturbance. The Media Information Officer of the Joint Task Force, Operation Enduring Peace, Captain Chinonso Oteh, said, “Yes, it is true. That one happened in the Jos North area.” James Abraham
